# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 4 (Bu-Vb Ss4)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Ss4
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 4
**Title (English, from literature):** Encouraging a woman to satisfy one’s desires

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Attakāmpāricariya* ("Encouraging a woman to satisfy one’s desires") constitutes the fourth *saṅghādisesa* training rule of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule legislates against sexual solicitation, establishing that a lustful monk who commends the servicing of his own passions to a woman—suggesting or recommending sexual congress—commits an offense requiring formal suspension and community rehabilitation (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its canonical analysis has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. None of the sampled secondary literature passages substantively analyze this text, as matching references represent internal section marks (§4) in unrelated modern scholarship.
The rule is shared universally across Buddhist monastic legal codes. SuttaCentral records full parallels in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, alongside matching Vibhaṅga and Prātimokṣa rules preserved across Northern traditions in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit recensions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus highlights extensive Pali-internal phrasing shared between this rule and related Vibhaṅga sections on sexual or bodily misconduct, including *Saṅghādisesa* 2 (Bu-Vb Ss2, with over 23,000 shared characters), *Saṅghādisesa* 3, and *Pārājika* rules 1 through 4, as well as multiple Khandhaka chapters [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with Tibetan canonical Vinaya literature (such as the *Vinayavibhaṅga*, D0003, and *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga*, D0005) and Sanskrit texts including Jayarakṣita's *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā*, agreeing with SuttaCentral on the wide cross-tradition transmission of these monastic legal definitions [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
